title: Cellular Automata
description: A grid of cells, each on or off, each following one rule from its neighbours. Most rules die out or freeze or boil into noise; a few, at the edge between order and chaos (Langton's λ near 0.27), make gliders, guns and machines. Von Neumann showed such a grid can hold a constructor that builds a copy of anything, itself included. Unlocks the Automaton Lattice: Von Neumann Constructors, and Quine Replicators far more cheaply.

puzzle.goal: In Conway's Life a cell lives on if it has two or three live neighbours. In a random grid with a fraction ρ of cells alive, the chance a cell has exactly k live neighbours of its eight is binomial. Write the chance P it has exactly three.
puzzle.name: Neighbours in Life
puzzle.ask: Find P for a grid with ρ = @{rho} of its cells alive.

vars.P: chance of exactly three live neighbours

puzzle.method: C(8,3) = 56 ways to choose which three of the eight are alive, each with ρ³(1 − ρ)⁵.
